name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,328

clue.text: Miles left sorrowful over girl's rejection

indicators.note: the miles have left, departed from the word they were in, so that letter goes
one word lies over and around the other, covering it

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for miles
dismal means gloomy, sorrowful
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Miles is upset because his girlfriend has rejected him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles' looks like a man's name, but it is the unit, and it has to leave before the girl goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is a sending away or turning down, so it is a synonym for rejection.

clue.text: Very small part of hybrid warfare

indicators.note: the letters wanted are only a part of the following phrase, sitting inside it

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A small detail of modern hybrid warfare, mixing cyber and conventional attack.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, dwarf describes a much smaller than usual variety, as in dwarf conifer, so it means very small.

clue.text: Odds on it's about strong criticism of flyers

indicators.note: one part sits about, around, the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: SP, starting price, is the odds offered on a horse at the off
taken as written, without the apostrophe
to come under fire is to be strongly criticised

explanation.surface: Betting odds on how airline pilots will take a fierce attack on their performance.
explanation.walkthrough: ITS goes about FIRE to make ITFIRES, and SP is put on the front. SP is betting shorthand for starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitfires were the famous British fighter planes of the Second World War, so they are examples of flyers.

clue.text: Arising from innate envy regardless of the circumstances

indicators.note: the answer arises out of these letters, emerging in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A statement that some behaviour comes from an inborn jealousy, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means whatever happens, at any rate, which is the same idea as regardless of the circumstances.

clue.text: City raised it with regard to joining second division

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
EC is the postcode of the City of London
taken as written, then turned upward
on means about, with regard to

explanation.surface: A city has raised a matter about joining a lower football division.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC. 'Second division' reads as one football league, but second is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is one of the parts something is divided into, so it is a synonym for division.

clue.text: Checked story covering American university department

indicators.note: one word covers the other, wrapping around it

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
D is an abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: A checked news story about a department at an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checked' could be a pattern or a verified story; here it means held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something checked has been held back or restricted, and limited means restricted in the same way.

clue.text: See file on German leader

indicators.note: a word's leader is the letter that leads it, its first
in an across clue, one thing written on another comes after it, so the file follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a rasp is a coarse file for wood or metal

explanation.surface: An instruction to look up the file on a German leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See file on' reads like a cross-reference; See is the definition and RASP sits on G.
explanation.definitionFit: To see in the sense of 'I see' is to understand, and to grasp an idea is to understand it too.

clue.text: Attract the attention of some passing rabbis

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying within them

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Trying to catch the eye of a few rabbis walking past.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something that grabs you catches your interest, so grab means attract the attention of.

clue.text: Conscious of Grant's interminable energy

indicators.note: interminable means without end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: an award is a grant, as of money
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone recognises the endless energy of a man called Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: AWARD loses its last letter and E is added. 'Grant' looks like a name, but it is a sum of money given.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware of something is to know about it or notice it, which is what being conscious of it means.

clue.text: Enter and catch informer packing to go

indicators.note: the preceding words are packed inside the next, like goods in a case

blocks.note: to net a fish is to catch it
a rat is an informer who betrays others
needing to go is a polite way of saying needing to urinate

explanation.surface: Police break in to catch a grass who is packing his bags to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: NET and RAT join and are packed into PEE. 'Packing to go' sounds like getting ready to leave, but 'to go' is the slang for using the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate a place is to get into it, so it is a synonym for enter.

clue.text: Start to agree over Amin's inner personality

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken
turned over, the name is read from right to left

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written, then turned around

explanation.surface: Beginning to agree about the inner character of the dictator Idi Amin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like 'about', but here it means the name is turned over. Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the soul or inner self, the inner personality turned towards the unconscious.

clue.text: What did you say about me living in Ohio once more?

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
O. is the traditional abbreviation for Ohio
taken as written
again means once more

explanation.surface: Someone asks to have repeated what was said about them living in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run C, O, ME, AGAIN; 'living in Ohio' places ME with the state's O. The definition is the whole question.
explanation.definitionFit: Come again? is an informal request for someone to repeat what they just said, like asking what did you say.

clue.text: It's just as likely to happen in the middle of Dallas

definitions.text: It's just as likely to happen

blocks.clueFragment: It's just as likely to happen in the middle of Dallas
blocks.note: surface reading: something with an even chance of occurring in a Texan city
setter's reading: the two central letters of Dallas are LL, and L is the Roman numeral for fifty, twice over

explanation.surface: An even chance that something will happen in downtown Dallas.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a plain definition of an even chance; the rest is a joke on the double L at the heart of Dallas, read as two Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome that is equally likely either way is called a half-and-half, even-money chance, exactly this expression.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

blocks.note: first meaning: crooked, corrupt
second meaning: a natural inclination or aptitude

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a leaning to crime, but the two words are separate meanings; 'criminal' is the adjective and 'tendency' the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for dishonest or corrupt, and it is also a noun meaning a natural inclination.

clue.text: Shuts road after Henry's narrow escape

indicators.note: the road is placed after Henry, so Henry's piece is written first

blocks.note: closes means shuts
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Ave is short for avenue, a road

explanation.surface: Henry nearly comes to grief when someone closes the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The road comes after Henry, so H precedes AVE. Henry looks like a man's name, but it is the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is an idiom for a near miss, a situation where disaster was only just avoided.

clue.text: A means of transport for gunmen in part of Ulster

indicators.note: one part is placed in the other, enclosed by it

blocks.note: Cavan is one of the nine counties of the province of Ulster, in the Irish Republic
the RA, Royal Artillery, are the army's gunners

explanation.surface: Smuggling a vehicle for terrorists into a county of Northern Ireland's province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunmen' suggests paramilitaries, but in crosswords it is the Royal Artillery. Cavan lies in the historic province, though not in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a towed trailer home, or a convoy of travellers, so it is one way of getting around.

clue.text: Complete article on church evacuation

blocks.note: clear means complete, as in a clear week
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A full report on the emptying of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearance is the removal of people or things from a place, the same act as an evacuation.

clue.text: Key to the Italian girl's predicament

blocks.note: D is a musical key
il is Italian for the
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The key that solves an Italian girl's awkward situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between two bad options, a kind of predicament.

clue.text: Manuscript includes vignette essentially on girl's endless memory aids

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so the central letters are kept
without an end, the final letter is dropped
the outer word includes the rest, holding it inside

blocks.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript
the two middle letters of an eight-letter word
Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A manuscript contains a vignette about a girl with a poor memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' means the heart of vignette, its middle pair, and the girl's name loses its final letter before the manuscript abbreviation wraps everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Mnemonics are devices such as rhymes or acronyms that help you remember things, so they are memory aids.

clue.text: A place on the outskirts of Crewe producing perfume

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
the first and last letters of the town

explanation.surface: A factory on the edge of Crewe, an English railway town, that makes scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A place' is vague on purpose: any town could do, and here it is the German city Essen. Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract of a plant's scent, and the word is used for perfume.

clue.text: Set forth without money

blocks.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
the pound is British money

explanation.surface: A traveller sets out with no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set forth' suggests a departure, but it means to explain in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound a theory is to present and explain it at length, which is what setting it forth means.

clue.text: Spartan writer eventually taken away by soldiers

indicators.note: what comes eventually comes at the end, and that last letter is taken away

blocks.note: Jane Austen, the novelist
the RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: A writer from Sparta was finally carried off by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' looks like a native of ancient Sparta, but it is the adjective for a plain, harsh life.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan living is plain and without comfort, just as an austere life is severe and simple.

clue.text: Flies volunteers back during struggle to occupy the centre of Damascus

indicators.note: going back, the word is read in the opposite direction
one word comes during the other, placed in its midst
to occupy a space is to sit inside it
only the central letters of the city's name are used

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve, here turned back
to vie is to struggle or compete
the two central letters of an eight-letter name

explanation.surface: Volunteers retreat while fighting to hold central Damascus in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a news report from Syria; the TA, Britain's Territorial Army, is the crossword's usual volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot an aircraft, a formal word for flying, so aviates means flies.

clue.text: Crack found in diamond

blocks.note: first meaning: crack cocaine, sold in lumps
second meaning: slang for a precious gem

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a flaw in a gemstone, but crack is the drug and both words are slang for the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is street slang for crack cocaine and informal slang for a diamond or other gem.

clue.text: Economic collapse caused by head of Coutts getting reckless

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
rash means reckless

explanation.surface: A financial meltdown caused by the boss of Coutts, a private British bank, taking wild risks.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a sudden fall in prices or a business failure, the kind of collapse an economy suffers.

clue.text: Turns to wine in misery

blocks.note: milk that turns spoils, goes off
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone takes to drink when they are unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misery' reads as unhappiness, but here it is a person: a misery is a gloomy killjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a misery means they are a wet blanket who spoils others' fun, which is what a spoilsport does.

clue.text: Right about demise of Vogue

indicators.note: turned about, the abbreviation faces the other way

blocks.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
a demise is an end, a death

explanation.surface: A claim about the end of the fashion magazine Vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vogue' with its capital looks like the magazine; it is the definition, meaning fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A vogue is the current fashion, and a trend is the prevailing direction of fashion, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Cliff's caught wearing women's clothing - not Poins

indicators.note: a letter wearing a garment is inside it
not means the setter's pronoun is left out

blocks.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a sari is a draped garment worn by women in South Asia
Poins is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A man called Cliff is caught cross-dressing, and the setter disowns him.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside SARI to make SCARI, then the setter's I is removed. Poins is the setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky cliff or crag, a word found mainly in northern English place names.

clue.text: Not wasting time on a story of little importance

indicators.note: wasting something means losing it, so that letter is lost from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
an account is a story or report of events

explanation.surface: A tale told without wasting time is not worth much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not wasting time' sounds like efficiency, but it tells you to drop a T.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-account person or thing is worthless or insignificant, an informal adjective for trivial.

clue.text: A fancy uniform

blocks.note: taken as written
to fancy something is to like it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy uniform' reads as dress uniform; fancy is the verb and uniform the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are uniform are all the same, without variation, which is what alike means.

clue.text: A number made from three

indicators.note: the answer is made from these letters, built up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sum showing how one number can be produced from three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' wants a numeral like three, but here a number is something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was used as an early anaesthetic, a substance that numbs patients, so it is a number in the numbing sense.

clue.text: Rickety side, ends and top finally gave out

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are knocked into a new order
finally points to the last letter of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wobbly piece of furniture whose sides, ends and top finally collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gave out' looks like collapsing, matching the rickety furniture, but it means handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or hand out, so dispensed means gave out in that sense.
